newsitem.title: USA: Intel sets $820 million profit-sharing plan.
newsitem.headline: Intel sets $820 million profit-sharing plan.

text.p: Intel Corp., the world's biggest maker of computer chips, said Tuesday its workers received about $820 million in cash bonuses, profit sharing and retirement pay for the company's record year in 1996.
Chief Operating Officer Craig Barrett also said all employees will now be eligible for stock options, starting in the next programme which will be launched in April.

"This outstanding year would not have been possible without the remarkable efforts of Intel employees around the world," said Barrett, who is slated to become president of Intel this spring, making him heir apparent to Chief Executive Officer Andy Grove.

Barrett said $214 million, or the equivalent of 26.9 days' pay for each Intel employee, was paid out under the Employee Cash Bonus Programme in 1996. All employees around the world receive the cash profit-sharing in six month instalments.

In 1996, the company also extended its Employee Bonus profitability-based programme to all employees. The plan, based on growth in Intel earnings and achievement of an employee's business group goals, paid out a total of $360 million.

Intel's previously announced special, one-time bonus for the company's record 1996 paid $1,000 apiece to U.S. employees and a locally adjusted figure for non-U.S. employees for a total of $45 million.
Intel also said that for the ninth straight year it contributed the maximum allowed by law to its employee retirement programme, or 12.5 percent of employees' pay, for a total of about $200 million.
